reasoning:
To find the characteristic polynomial of a matrix $ A $, we compute $ \det(\lambda I - A) $, where $ \lambda $ is a scalar and $ I $ is the identity matrix. The given matrix is:

$$
A = \begin{pmatrix}
-4 & -13 & 10 \\
-9 & 10 & 4 \\
12 & -5 & -14
\end{pmatrix}
$$

Subtracting $ \lambda $ from the diagonal entries gives:

$$
\lambda I - A = \begin{pmatrix}
\lambda + 4 & 13 & -10 \\
9 & \lambda - 10 & -4 \\
-12 & 5 & \lambda + 14
\end{pmatrix}
$$

The determinant of this matrix is calculated using cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$
\det(\lambda I - A) = (\lambda + 4)\begin{vmatrix} \lambda - 10 & -4 \\ 5 & \lambda + 14 \end{vmatrix} - 13\begin{vmatrix} 9 & -4 \\ -12 & \lambda + 14 \end{vmatrix} + (-10)\begin{vmatrix} 9 & \lambda - 10 \\ -12 & 5 \end{vmatrix}
$$

Computing each minor:

1. $ \begin{vmatrix} \lambda - 10 & -4 \\ 5 & \lambda + 14 \end{vmatrix} = (\lambda - 10)(\lambda + 14) - (-4)(5) = \lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 140 + 20 = \lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120 $
2. $ \begin{vmatrix} 9 & -4 \\ -12 & \lambda + 14 \end{vmatrix} = 9(\lambda + 14) - (-4)(-12) = 9\lambda + 126 - 48 = 9\lambda + 78 $
3. $ \begin{vmatrix} 9 & \lambda - 10 \\ -12 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 9(5) - (\lambda - 10)(-12) = 45 + 12\lambda - 120 = 12\lambda - 75 $

Substituting back:

$$
\det(\lambda I - A) = (\lambda + 4)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) - 13(9\lambda + 78) - 10(12\lambda - 75)
$$

Expanding and simplifying:

1. $ (\lambda + 4)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) = \lambda^3 + 4\lambda^2 - 120\lambda + 4\lambda^2 + 16\lambda - 480 = \lambda^3 + 8\lambda^2 - 104\lambda - 480 $
2. $ -13(9\lambda + 78) = -117\lambda - 1014 $
3. $ -10(12\lambda - 75) = -120\lambda + 750 $

Combining all terms:

$$
\lambda^3 + 8\lambda^2 - 104\lambda - 480 - 117\lambda - 1014 - 120\lambda + 750 = \lambda^3 + 8\lambda^2 - 341\lambda - 744
$$

Thus, the characteristic polynomial is $ \lambda^3 + 8\lambda^2 - 341\lambda - 744 $.
